spec.title: codkit PROP-006: Apply metadata, locking, inventory

status.comment: patch-set runtime metadata, locking, inventory and completeness

apply-metadata.title: 1. Apply metadata: the cache + the mark (the truth is the tree itself)

p.TREE-IS-TRUTH: **The truth about the applied state is the tree itself**: the generated branch, its tip and the commit trailers (`Codkit-Patchset-Commit`, `Codkit-Upstream-Pin`). The metadata is a cache that can always be thrown away; losing it means «apply from scratch» and never an interactive question.

facts.DELTA-FINGERPRINT:
**The delta fingerprint** (`deltaFingerprint`) is the hex sha256 of a canonical string: for every file under `delta/` recursively (the paths sorted by their UTF-8 bytes) — the line `<path-from-the-patchset-root>
<sha256 of the content in hex>
`; plus the closing lines `pin <pin.sha>
schema 1
`. Own code enters through its own files under `delta/own/`.
facts.TREE-ID: **The identity of the tree** (`treeId`) is the hex sha256 of the realpath of the root of the tree (the normalized absolute path after the symlinks are resolved), its first 16 hex characters.
facts.CACHE-FILE: **The cache in the patch set** is the file `.codkit/trees/<treeId>.json`: `codkitTreeCache: 1`; `treePath` (the realpath, for diagnostics); `treeRepoAnchor` (the confirmed `upstreamAnchorCommit`); `pinSha`; `deltaFingerprint`; `branchTip` (the SHA of the tip of the generated branch); `updatedAt` (ISO).
facts.TREE-MARK: **The mark in the tree** is the file `codkit/applied.json` in the per-worktree git directory (`git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`; in an ordinary tree — `<tree>/.git/codkit/applied.json`, in a linked worktree — the per-worktree directory, not the common dir: every worktree has a mark of its own; it survives `clean -fdx` and is invisible to status): `{"codkitTreeMark":1,"pinSha":…,"deltaFingerprint":…,"branchTip":…,"ownFingerprint":…}`. The fields `ownFingerprint` (the hash of the own subtree at the moment of the `load`) and `ownFiles` (a map `path → sha256` of the own files at the moment of the `load`; added by the M0 implementation) are needed by the guard to tell apart, file by file, «the patch set was edited» / «the tree was edited» / «both sides were edited» (`##PATCHSET-SIDE-EDIT-RULE` PROP-008 §4). The fields of Phase 7 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign (decisions D16/D17, S0.9): `artifacts` — a map `path → sha256` of all the `delta/` files outside `delta/own/**` at the moment of the load (one traversal shared with the fingerprint — `deltaFiles()`; excluding own is the single filter `deltaArtifactMap`, and the writer of the mark and the reader of the check both go through it) — and `patchSetCommit`, the patch-set commit the load represented (`sha` | `dirty` | `none`; the value is the same one the `Codkit-Patchset-Commit` trailer of the built commits carries — the mark answers the case of an empty patch set, where there is no trailer). Both are `.optional()` in the schema: a mark written before them is read without them, and the shift check then honestly answers «unknown» (R13, PROP-008 `##PATCHSET-MOVED-RULE`); every write of the mark writes both. On a read-only mounted tree the mark is not written (a write error into `.git` is not fatal, the warning `CK-W-MARK-RO`).
facts.INPUTS-STAMP: **The stamp of the inputs** is the file `codkit/inputs.json` in the per-worktree git directory of the tree, beside the mark: `{"codkitInputs": 1, "inputs": [{"name", "to", "mode": "working|pinned", "commit": "<sha40>|null", "stamp": "<sha256>", "files": {"<path under from>": "<blob id>"}}]}`, the inputs in the order of the declaration and the files in the byte order of their paths, rewritten by every `load` that delivers inputs (PROP-008 `INPUTS-LOAD`). `stamp` is the sha256 of what the input takes - its commands, dependency roots, variables and `from`, never its location or `to` - and of its source: every file of a working tree with its blob id, or the pinned commit and its tree. A build is skipped when the stamp of an input in this run equals the recorded stamp of the same name and mode and the object database of the tree still holds every recorded blob: the recorded files are then the output (PROP-007 `INPUTS-BUILD`). The blobs stay unreferenced in the object database; a `git gc` that prunes them makes the next load build again. A stamp that does not read is a warning, and every input is built again: it is a record of codkit's own writing, never a source of truth.
facts.CONSUMED-REFS: **The consumed tree commits** — `refs/codkit/consumed/<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<short7>` → the former HEAD of the tree: the write `recordConsumedRef` (the module `lib/treeCommits.ts`, the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, decision D6) is performed under the lock of the common repository — the refs are shared by all the worktrees of the repository (PROP-008 `##GENERATED-REF-WORKTREE-PREFLIGHT`). They are created when the tree commits are consumed by an extraction (the `save` of the later phases) or discarded explicitly (`load --discard`). The refs are diagnostics, not the truth (`##TREE-IS-TRUTH`): only `gc` cleans them (decision D22), they are never touched by hand; they are reachable from any worktree of the repository.
facts.SYNC-TRANSACTION-FILE: **The transaction file of the two-way `sync`** is `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` in the root of the patch set (the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, Phase 8, decision D20; the module `lib/syncTransaction.ts`, the algorithm is PROP-008 §5a `##SYNC-TRANSACTION`). It is written by `writeContainedFileExclusive` before the first mutation of the run (a second start over a live record is impossible by construction), atomically rewritten after every atom (a patch-set commit — with the trailer `Codkit-Sync-Transaction: <id>` — and the consumed ref are appended to the record) and removed after the last one. It carries: both HEADs, `markSnapshot` (the mark as it was found), `dirtyBefore`, the `hash-object -w` snapshots of everything the run will overwrite, `patchsetCommits`, `consumedRef`, `conflicts` — `[{path, materialized}]` (Phase 8b: the sha256 of the written markers, or `null` — the merge did not reach the file; `status` prints `conflicts: N` from this field and `--continue` checks completeness against it). While the file exists: `load`/`save`/`sync` (step 0 of every call of the engines) refuse with `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` (exit 1) and `status` prints `sync in progress: <id>, conflicts: N`. The ownership protocol is its own (F24): it is touched neither by hand nor by `gc` (D22 lists it and explains why); a refusal without a single write removes the file itself (the proof is a comparison of the snapshots and of HEAD, not a guess), while a refusal or a crash after a write leaves it for the recovery by `--abort`/`--continue` (Phase 8b, D21; the audit of `--abort` and the restoration from the snapshots are PROP-008 §5a). A broken or foreign file is fail closed: a refusal, not a guess.

p.GC-CLASSES: **The classes of `codkit gc`** (the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, Phase 9, decision D22; the module `lib/gc.ts`, the command is PROP-007 `##CMD-GC`). gc takes the lock of the tree, prints the plan — every candidate with its class and its remove/keep action, the kept ones included — and removes **only** a closed list of classes: `refs/codkit/consumed/*` older than N days beyond the last n (`--keep-consumed n`, default 5; `--older-than days`, default 30; the refs are shared by all the worktrees, hence the removal under the lock of the common repository); `.codkit/tmp/*` — the scratch of runs whose `finally` did not execute (a per-tree scratch `<treeId>.index|.blob` whose lock owner is alive stays); a tree lock with a dead owner (the pid in the file is not alive; the release goes through the acquisition protocol with a choice of generation, not a bare unlink; a stale lock of **its own** tree is released by the acquisition itself, as it is today — ##LOCK-MECHANISM §2, and gc names that release in the plan); a `.codkit/trees/<id>.json` whose `treePath` does not exist; `.codkit/out/*`. **It never touches**: `.codkit/locks/daemon-*` and `.codkit/build/*` (their own protocol of a provable owner, REPAIR-011; the cleanup of the daemon logs is DEF-9), the transactions and the receipts — `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` (##SYNC-TRANSACTION-FILE), `.codkit/rename-transaction.json`, `.codkit/rename-completions/`, `.codkit/rebase-onto-pin/` — and `.codkit/pending/*`: gc only lists them with an explanation of why they are kept. It does not touch the Git objects of the tree (a `git gc` on the tree is a human decision). `--dry-run` prints the same plan without removing anything; `--json` gives `data.plan`, `data.removed`, `data.kept`. Directories are not cleaned blindly: every entry is classified by its name and removed one at a time.

p.FAST-PATH-RULE: **The comparison rule (a fast no-op `load`)** — it is allowed only when ALL of the conditions are true: the cache exists ∧ the `pinSha`/`deltaFingerprint` of the cache equal the current ones ∧ the branch `codkit/applied/<pin.tag>` exists in the tree ∧ its tip == the `branchTip` of the cache ∧ the HEAD of the tree points at it ∧ (the mark is absent ∨ the mark matches). Any mismatch → a full bring-up from scratch. A stale cache cannot be taken for the truth by construction.

p.MULTI-TREE-SUPPORT: Multiple trees are supported: the cache records are keyed by `treeId`; concurrent access is protected by the lock (§2); a tree swapped under a live cache must lead to a full re-application (scenario S15 of FEAT-002).

p.LOCK-MECHANISM: The file `.codkit/locks/<treeId>.lock` in the patch set is created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and holds `{pid, startedAt, command}`. Every writing command takes it; `status`/`where`/`inventory` work without the lock (the read-only path). A stale lock (the process with that pid does not exist) is released automatically with a warning. A second process gets exit 2 `CK-E-LOCKED` with the pid and a hint. `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EROFS` while creating the lock is an environment refusal 2 `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` that demands a separate writable `.codkit` mount; the source patch set may stay read-only in that case. A shared tree in CI is additionally protected by the fingerprint (a mark mismatch → a full re-application).

p.INVENTORY-IS-GENERATED: The inventory is **generated** by the tool from the `delta/**` artifacts and the marker annotation; it is not kept by hand and is not committed as a source of truth. The output is `.codkit/out/inventory.json` (+ `--md` for a human); the generated version and its diff between two states are published into the CI artifacts and for the review (we review the changes of the inventory, not the patch files).

facts.INVENTORY-SORTED: `entries` are sorted by `id`; the metrics are derived; the serialization is deterministic.
facts.INVENTORY-METRIC-TARGET: The main metric is `patchAndRuleCount` per subsystem (rewrite-rule + patch). Every completed cycle writes a snapshot of the metrics into its committed journal; the aggregated time series is a derived report and requires no separate CSV in the tool repository.
facts.INVENTORY-ROUTING: Routing: the subsystem of an intervention → the set of tests and the owner (the owners map) — from the inventory; the review checklist of the cycle is generated from it as well (it is not hard-coded).

facts.IB-READ-ARTIFACTS: Read and validate against the schemas: all the `.ckpatch` (their headers), the overlays, the resource map, the rules, `patchset.delta.json`, `removed.json`, `owners.json`.
facts.IB-MAKE-ENTRIES: For every artifact — an inventory entry: `subsystem` = the second component of the id; `files` = the target or targets of the artifact; `artifact` = the path of the artifact file.
facts.IB-METRICS: The metrics are aggregates over the entries; the serialization is deterministic (the entries are sorted by id).

p.IB-SPEED: The speed requirement: a build over the full volume takes seconds; the patches are parsed without touching the tree; the tree is needed only by the cross-checks (§5–6).

hunks-in-markers.title: 5. «Every hunk inside a marker» — the matching

p.him-io: The input: the patch P of the file F; the content of F in the **target state** (the pin + P — computed by applying P to the content of the pin in memory with our own implementation of `applyUnified` with an exact context match: there are no shifts on our own pin — by construction the patch is regenerated against the pin).

hunks-in-markers.fence: checkHunksInsideMarkers(P, pinBytes): targetBytes = applyUnified(pinBytes, P) blocks = parseMarkers(targetBytes, ext(F)).blocks for each hunk h in P: for each added line a (position in the target numbering): if a is not covered by any block -> CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER (file, line) for each removed line d: -> CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-LINE (file, line in the pin numbering) # exception: the line is removed AND its commented-out copy is added inside a block by the # same hunk («neutralization by commenting out»). The check: among the added lines of the # hunk there is a line whose text = commentForm(ext) + the text of the removed line (up to # the leading whitespace indent). Then it is admissible. the marker lines of the blocks themselves must be added lines of this same patch (there are no upstream markers); a block without a single added line other than the markers -> the warning CK-W-EMPTY-BLOCK

p.MARKER-ARTIFACT-CONSISTENCY: The consistency «marker ↔ artifact»: the id of every block in the target state of the file = the id of the patch of that file (for entry-module — an id from the list of the patches of the layer); the id of the patch must be present among the blocks. A violation is `CK-E-MARKER-ARTIFACT-MISMATCH`.

p.ADD-FILE-EXEMPTION: An add-file patch (the whole file consists of added lines) is not subject to the «every hunk inside a marker» check — there are no upstream lines to protect; only the validity of the markers of the file and the consistency «block ↔ artifact id» apply to it (a clarification of M0). A new file whose extension has no marker form carries no block, and that is a legal state of it, not the refusal a patched upstream file without a comment syntax gets: the locale manifests of an extension are JSON (decision of 2026-11-01; `save --allow-new-file` and `verify` read such a file as block-free).

p.NEUTRALIZATION-DETAILS: Clarifications of the «neutralization by commenting out» (the M0 implementation): the comment wrapper is an ORDINARY comment of the language (the marker form minus the word `codkit:`: `// `, `/* … */`, `<!-- … -->`, `# `), and the closing half is mandatory for CSS/HTML; the comparison of the text trims the leading spaces and tabs on both sides and the trailing ones on the wrapper; the commented-out copy must lie in the SAME hunk as the removal. A `-`/`+` pair that edits an upstream line in place (rather than commenting it out) is `CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-LINE` by construction (the rule `##MR-FUNCTIONAL-ONLY` of PROP-004: upstream lines are commented out, not edited) — the most frequent expected signal of this check, and not a false one.

p.NO-NEWLINE-MARKER-SEMANTICS: The semantics of `\ No newline at end of file` in `applyUnified`: after a `-` line the marker asserts the state of the pin (a mismatch is the refusal `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN`), after a `+` line it sets the state of the result, and after a context line it does both.

p.COMPLETENESS-CHECK: The input: the tree in the applied state (the tip of the generated branch) and the pin. The algorithm: `git diff --name-status <pin.sha> <branchTip>` → the list of the changed paths. Every path must be explained by exactly one source: the own directory (`src/vs/<ownDirName>/**` — only in the CI/publish mode, locally own is not in the commits), a patch with that target path, an overlay target, a resource-map target. An unexplained path → `CK-E-UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION`. Conversely: an artifact whose target is not changed in the diff → `CK-E-STALE-ARTIFACT` (an empty patch, for instance) — with the M1 reservation for overlays: a local `load` materializes an overlay through the dev channel only, so overlay targets DO explain a changed path but are NOT obliged to be present in the diff. The absence of the generated branch is not a failure of completeness but a skipped check with the warning «run codkit load first» (verify works otherwise).

p.REMOVED-NOT-AN-ENTRY: The entries of the removed registry are NOT inventory entries (the kind is not a layer): they do not enter `entries`, but they do enter the requirements of the guard coverage (`contractCoverage.requiredTotal` may exceed the number of guard-obliged entries) and are checked by verify (a clarification of M1).
